title: The Legion of the Radiant Flame
type: Fein Uaill · freedom, courage and exploration
dek: A legion of warriors and explorers seeking lives of their own making, with a shared flame that becomes painfully contested when its dead return.

chapters.title: Zeke and the life beyond the harbor
The stolen flame is a story people argue about

body:
The Radiant Flame wants a life that is lived boldly. For Arandiel that means being willing to fight at the front; for the sailor Zeke it means stepping onto an uncharted island and giving it a name. Its promise of freedom binds people to a proud mortal tradition. Elenia’s service, and the crisis over bringing soldiers back, show how costly that bond can become.

Compare the four factions → · All factions → · Fein Uaill →

Freedom that must be defended

The Legion’s stated ideals are glory, freedom and personal strength. It values courage, merit and ambition, opposing the claim that old elites are naturally superior. High Lady Liraeth Dawnbringer is its named leader. The free peoples it imagines are joined by respect and the strength to defend their liberty.

Its code asks members to prove themselves, meet challenges and claim mortal strength as their own rather than credit the gods. These commitments are demanding, especially when a member’s loyalties pull in different directions. Arandiel presents joining and sacrifice as choices: her people fight because they love their land, not because someone has offered them up against their will.

Zeke and the life beyond the harbor

The Shining Shores are the island’s busy point of arrival, principally influenced by the Legion. Its work reaches beyond the training ground. On the cultural tour, Zeke shows Elenia and Wren the fleet being prepared and describes exploration followed by Emerald Veil study under the explorers’ protection.

Zeke says a captain let him name a newly charted island after he helped save that captain in a storm. The pride belongs to a common sailor, not a court pedigree. His account of Ezekenine is a personal story of earned opportunity; it supplies no new surveyed map coordinates.

He finds the Silver Star’s concern for old lives less compelling than the chance to live his own. He wants to look back in wonder at what he has done. His enthusiasm makes the Legion’s appeal specific: ships, family, discovery and an avenue for a person with little status to do something memorable.

The stolen flame is a story people argue about

Zeke recounts a legend in which Cala abandons the people and young mortals steal her flame from the heavenly realm. He attributes the old account to Silver Star history. Asked about the flame, he allows that he personally understands it as an allegory.

Wren questions why people accept so consequential a story without probing it. Her doubt and Zeke’s affection for it can both remain in the record. Neither a sailor’s retelling nor a visitor’s suspicion establishes the complete objective history of Cala’s relationship with Zarathis.

The faction is called the Legion of the Radiant Flame in its faction description. Some speakers and appearances use Radiant Dawn, including Zeke’s title and Liraeth’s nomination speech. Those names are retained as recorded variants here, without inventing a fifth Fein Uaill faction or a separate founding event.

Elenia joins by choice

At Aelthor, Elenia asks what joining would require. Arandiel recognizes her battlefield conduct and offers her a place as Knight Elenia of the Radiant Flame. Arandiel’s welcome recognizes what Elenia has already done in their defense.

At the later readiness exercise, Elenia rallies her soldiers with the promise of victory and drinks together afterward. The narrator identifies them as fellow Radiant Flame members responding eagerly to one of their own. Her excitement fits the fellowship Zeke describes.

Elenia’s devotion to Cala does not vanish when she joins. Both her welcomed service and the Legion’s rejection of divine dependence shape the conflict that follows.

Arandiel: advance, judgment and cost

At the readiness exercise, Arandiel tests the ability to achieve an objective rather than merely kill opponents. She warns against wasting soldiers and insists that those who give their lives deserve respect. Eugene wins the relic despite her expectation that Elenia or Wren would prevail. She recognizes his success and lets him keep it. Boldness remains a preference; it does not permit her to rewrite the outcome.

At the Void expedition, Radiant Flame warriors accompany the scholars. Arandiel argues that progress has a cost and urges the company onward even when she is nearly overcome by exhaustion. Her courage and her readiness to keep advancing are visible together. The account does not require every cost to become necessary simply because she says sacrifice is worthwhile.

These scenes give military merit a sharper meaning than a ladder of ranks: care for troops, judgment under competition, acknowledgment of someone else’s success and the difficulty of knowing when to stop.

Liraeth chooses a warrior

After Aria’s death, Liraeth appears in full armor and names Arandiel as the faction’s candidate. She invokes the courage to lead as Aria did. Arandiel’s own appeal rests on fighting and bleeding for Zarathis, presenting leadership as something demonstrated in action.

This endorsement sits beside rival choices of Wren, Magnus and Lucent. It does not make Arandiel the automatic ruler, make Aria the formal head of all four factions or settle the election before votes are counted. Aria’s cultural and military stature is the legacy the candidates are answering.

When the soldiers come back

At the memorial in the Month of Hope, Year 2, the Radiant Flame is responsible for rites preserving the spirit of the dead. Arandiel describes its living flame as the people’s spirit, something that should never die. Elenia asks to use it to honor their fallen soldiers.

The restoration that follows breaks open the difference between honoring the dead and bringing them home. Arandiel sees her soldiers returned through divine power and cannot reconcile the joy with the boundary she has been taught. She hands the torch to Magnus and collapses in tears. Her response is grief and conflict, not a simple victory for either side of the argument.

Magnus asks Bowene to strip Elenia of her Radiant Flame standing. A request for punishment is not the punishment itself. The later duel, alteration of Magnus’s face and exile are told in Elenia’s continuing history. The public faction record preserves both her earlier admission and this rupture; a final membership ruling remains unestablished here.
